underground_mines_meta_description: Underground Mines was a Vintage Story mod that generated huge underground mine networks with ores, loot and danger.
underground_mines_hero_lead: Huge mines beneath your feet. Sometimes a little too huge.
underground_mines_hero_description: A procedural generation mod that filled Vintage Story's underground with connected galleries, ores, loot and creatures. Getting in was the easy part.
underground_mines_generation_title: It did not place a mine. It grew one.
underground_mines_generation_description: The mod combined prepared pieces with generation rules to build a different network in every world. Galleries continued through new chunks and could reach a fairly unreasonable scale.
underground_mines_generation_entrances_d: Mines could announce themselves on the surface or connect to caves. You could also find them the traditional way: digging down and having faith.
underground_mines_generation_galleries_d: Corridors, crossings, turns and shafts were combined procedurally to extend the structure without relying on a closed map.
underground_mines_generation_rooms_descr: Special rooms distributed resources, loot and hostile encounters so exploring the network involved more than following empty tunnels.
underground_mines_network_alt: Distant view of a Vintage Story world revealing a huge mine network generated beneath the terrain
underground_mines_network_caption: Remove the terrain and the whole trick appears: a network crossing mountains, lakes and valleys without asking permission.
underground_mines_world_title: The mine had to feel like part of the world.
underground_mines_world_description: Generation did more than paste structures. It read the terrain context to adapt materials, resources and danger to the place where each mine appeared.
underground_mines_rule_rock: Mine blocks adapted to the local rock type instead of looking as though they had been imported from another world.
underground_mines_rule_ores: Ores respected which deposits could exist in that rock, preserving the game's prospecting logic.
underground_mines_rule_danger: Drifters, locusts and other encounters could occupy galleries and special rooms.
underground_mines_rule_config: Depth, entrances, additional ores and other elements could be adjusted through configuration.
underground_mines_technical_description: The challenge was not drawing a nice tunnel. It was making many pieces connect across chunks, survive saved games and preserve the world's internal logic.
underground_mines_technical_code_title: C# and the Vintage Story API
underground_mines_technical_code_descrip: The mod's logic integrated with world generation to decide where, when and how to create each segment.
underground_mines_technical_schematics_d: Entrances, crossings, shafts, endings and mine variants acted as reusable pieces for composing each network.
underground_mines_technical_world_descri: Saved data allowed structures to continue across chunks and preserved generation decisions when the world was loaded again.
underground_mines_technical_server_descr: Generation ran on the server, so multiplayer worlds could include the mines without installing a client interface.
underground_mines_gallery_title: The scale changes with your point of view.
underground_mines_gallery_description: From inside, it was an abandoned mine. From outside, a tangle of galleries determined to occupy half the map.
underground_mines_gallery_interior_alt: Dark interior of a large mine room generated by Underground Mines in Vintage Story
underground_mines_gallery_network_alt: Aerial view of a Vintage Story world with Underground Mines' extensive underground network visible

liporca_hero_description: A Galician liqueur brand that decided to speak to its generation without giving up the product it's always made. The website had to do exactly the same: sell, tell the story, and not sound like the brochure for a rural guesthouse.
liporca_toast_alt: Four people toasting with the four liqueurs of Liporca
modereta_arch_deploy_description: Docker Compose brings together the bot and database; continuous integration checks formatting, linting, types and tests before accepting anything.
modereta_delivery_description: The new foundation includes containers for the bot and PostgreSQL, data migrations, command synchronisation and a suite of automated checks. Because “it runs on my machine” is information, not a production strategy.
modereta_demo_description: A sample of the flow, not a screenshot of the bot.
modereta_arch_rules_description: Behaviours that react to other bots live separately from commands. This lets Modereta listen without turning the main file into a mess.
modereta_demo_notice_description: Only people who saved this series or character will be mentioned.
modereta_flow_notify_title: Alert when there is a match
modereta_flow_kicker: A list, a drop, a notice

modereta_flow_save_title: Save what you are looking for
modereta_flow_save_description: Each person can maintain a list of favourite series and characters through commands with autocomplete.
modereta_flow_description: People only choose their favourites. Modereta reads Sofi's messages, normalises the names, cross-references the data and sends the alert when needed. The invisible work is the whole point.
modereta_flow_watch_description: A passive rule detects the drops of another bot, interprets the cards, and saves series, characters, and context.
modereta_rewrite_title: The same name. A base that is no longer scary to touch.
modereta_hero_lead: A bot that watches the drops so you do not have to keep staring at the chat.

vsds_idea_title: The server is replaceable. Your world is not.
vsds_hero_lead: A Vintage Story server. One command. Zero strange rituals.
vsds_security_title: It does not run as root. And that is good news.

vsl_hero_lead: Vintage Story, with multiple versions and without turning each installation into an archaeological excavation.

vsl_versions_description: Install different versions of Vintage Story with a couple of clicks and update them without repeating the whole process.

xvelte_code_title: A component already in the project
xvelte_code_footer: Normal, editable code with no magic hidden on another server.

xvelte_demo_description: The components on this page are xvelte too. Self-referential, but usefully so.
xvelte_area_visual_description: Tokens, light and dark themes, global styles and semantic icons that maintain a common language without tying the design.
xvelte_idea_description_2: You can change the structure, styles, dependencies or behaviour without waiting for a new package option. In return, you are also responsible for what you copy. Freedom, with an instruction manual. Fair enough.
xvelte_hero_lead: The pieces I always ended up building again. Now they all live in the same drawer.
xvelte_hero_description: A personal collection of components, hooks, attachments, styles and utilities for building interfaces with SvelteKit. Copy them into your project, adapt them and they become yours. No need to wrestle with someone else's API to move three pixels.

xvelte_meta_description: xvelte is a personal collection of reusable components, hooks, attachments, styles, and utilities for building applications and websites with SvelteKit.
xvelte_preferences_description: A small sample, not a full application packed into a card.
xvelte_idea_title: Copying is not the last resort. It is the model.
xvelte_step_adapt_description: Adapt the code to the application without getting trapped in an API designed for everyone.
xvelte_real_title: Made for projects, not for an eternal demo.
xvelte_real_image_alt: View of the xvelte documentation used as the collection's test bed

service_web_overview_description: Before discussing design or technology, we need to understand what is not working and who will use the website. A business that is not explaining itself clearly, a site that has lost credibility and an idea without a home of its own all need different solutions.
service_web_problem: A slow, confusing, outdated or uneditable website loses trust and opportunities. Being online is not enough: the website must explain the business clearly, guide each visit and make the next step easy.
service_web_audience: Businesses, professionals and projects that need a new website, a proper rebuild or a specific web tool without relying on a generic theme that tries to fit everything and does nothing particularly well.

service_web_includes_description: The scope adapts to the project, but it is always clear what will be prepared, what you need to provide and what you will receive at the end.
service_web_include_structure_descriptio: I organise pages, information hierarchy and journeys so people can find what they need without resorting to archaeology.
service_web_include_design_description: An interface consistent with your brand and prepared for mobile, desktop and everything in between. Accessibility and readability are included, not patched in at the end.
service_web_include_development_descript: Forms, analytics, content management, bookings, search or connections to other tools according to the project's actual needs.
service_web_include_launch_description: Domain and hosting configuration, performance, basic technical SEO, analytics and a clear explanation of how everything works before the job is considered finished.

service_web_faq_1_question: How much does a website cost?
service_web_faq_1_answer: It depends on the number of pages, features, content and design work required. Before giving a figure, I review the scope and separate what is essential from what can wait for a second phase.
service_web_faq_2_answer: It mainly depends on the scope and whether the content is ready. Before starting, we agree on realistic stages and deadlines; promising a date without reviewing anything would be quicker, but also fairly useless.
service_web_faq_3_question: Do I need to provide the copy and images?

service_web_faq_4_question: Will I be able to update the website myself?
service_web_faq_4_answer: Yes. Where the project calls for it, I provide a clear management area and explain how to use it. If you do not need frequent content updates, we also avoid installing an admin panel merely so we can say it exists.
service_web_faq_5_question: Do you include the domain, hosting and SEO?
service_web_faq_5_answer: I can configure the domain, email, hosting, deployment, analytics and technical SEO foundation. Third-party accounts remain in your name and their costs are listed separately.
service_web_faq_6_question: Do you only work with clients in Galicia?

service_ecommerce_short: E-commerce with a clear catalogue, reliable payments and day-to-day management that does not require a developer for every change.
service_ecommerce_meta_description: Online stores built with Shopify, WooCommerce or bespoke solutions for businesses selling products and services from Galicia.
service_ecommerce_lead: I build and improve online stores so finding, understanding and buying a product — and managing the resulting order — is straightforward for both sides.
service_ecommerce_hero_description: Online stores built with Shopify, WooCommerce or bespoke development for businesses that need to sell without complicating the purchase or day-to-day management. Based in Galicia and working remotely too.
service_ecommerce_overview_description: Selling online connects catalogue, content, payments, delivery and customer service. When one of those pieces does not fit, either the business or the person trying to buy pays for the friction. Sometimes both, just to keep things fair.
service_ecommerce_problem: A catalogue without structure, product pages that leave questions unanswered, costs that appear at the last moment or awkward administration turn every sale into a small obstacle course. The store must simplify both the purchase and the work that begins when an order arrives.
service_ecommerce_audience: Brands, retailers and businesses that want to begin selling online, migrate an existing store or bring order to a catalogue that grew without a plan. This includes direct-to-consumer sales and professional ordering.
service_ecommerce_purchase_description: A store is more than a product grid and a pay button. The journey must work before, during and after the purchase.
service_ecommerce_purchase_catalogue_des: Categories, collections, filters and search designed around how customers buy, not the internal order of a spreadsheet.
service_ecommerce_purchase_product_descr: Information, variants, photography and content organised so the product is easy to understand without opening another tab to investigate.
service_ecommerce_purchase_checkout_desc: Payment methods, delivery, taxes and conditions shown at the right time. A last-minute shock is a remarkably effective cart-abandonment strategy.
service_ecommerce_purchase_orders_descri: Statuses, notifications, stock, returns and daily operations prepared so selling more does not mean losing control behind the scenes.
service_ecommerce_start_title: Launch a store or bring order to the one you have.
service_ecommerce_start_description: A new project lets us design the foundation carefully. An active store has data, URLs, customers and sales that need protecting before anything changes.
service_ecommerce_new_description: For businesses beginning to sell online or needing to separate a new store from a website that has reached its limits.

service_ecommerce_new_point_2: Platform selection based on operations, budget and growth.

service_ecommerce_existing_point_2: Migration with redirects and checks to protect information.

service_ecommerce_faq_1_answer: It depends on the catalogue, budget, integrations and who will manage the store. I recommend the option that reduces medium-term problems, not whichever platform is fashionable that week.
service_ecommerce_faq_2_question: Can you migrate my existing store?
service_ecommerce_faq_2_answer: Yes. I review products, customers, orders, URLs, content and integrations before preparing a checked migration with redirects, so information and search visibility are protected.
service_ecommerce_faq_3_answer: We can agree a complete initial upload, an import, or a structure and training for your team to continue. It is defined before the work is priced.
service_ecommerce_faq_4_question: Can it connect to payment, delivery or invoicing services?
service_ecommerce_faq_4_answer: Yes, provided the supplier offers a suitable integration or API. I review limitations, external costs and the data that can be synchronised before promising magic based on three paragraphs of documentation.
service_ecommerce_faq_5_question: Do you provide maintenance after launch?
service_ecommerce_faq_5_answer: I can provide maintenance, support and ongoing improvements, but there is no compulsory commitment. The store, accounts and access remain in your name.
service_ecommerce_faq_6_question: Is an online store worthwhile for a small catalogue?
service_ecommerce_faq_6_answer: It can be, but it depends on margins, purchase frequency, logistics and how customers find you. If a simpler solution fits better, I will tell you before building anything.
service_custom_software_short: Internal tools, platforms and integrations built around the way your business actually works.
service_custom_software_meta_description: Bespoke software development for businesses: internal tools, platforms, integrations and solutions for specialist processes.
service_custom_software_lead: When a spreadsheet is crying for help and generic tools force the business to adapt around them, I design software around the real process.
service_custom_software_hero_description: Internal tools, platforms, APIs and integrations for businesses whose processes do not fit a generic product. Development from Galicia and remotely.
service_custom_software_overview_descrip: Bespoke software makes sense when it solves a specific business constraint, not when it merely replaces a blue form with a pink one. First we need to understand the process, the people using it and the real cost of carrying on as before.
service_custom_software_problem: Duplicating data, copying information between tools, losing track of work and relying on manual processes creates errors, wastes time and makes it hard to know what is happening. As the business grows, the workaround stops being small but remains a workaround.
service_custom_software_audience: Businesses and teams with a specialist process that does not fit a standard product, systems that need connecting because they currently ignore each other, or an internal tool that the business has outgrown.
service_custom_software_decision_title: Adapt what exists or build what is needed.
service_custom_software_decision_descrip: Building your own software is not always the best answer. The decision depends on the process, the cost of current limitations and how much that way of working differentiates the business.
service_custom_software_existing_descrip: When a product already solves most of the problem, configuring it, connecting it or adding a small custom layer will often make more sense.
service_custom_software_existing_point_1: Lower investment and a faster launch.
service_custom_software_existing_point_2: Integrations or extensions focused on what is missing.
service_custom_software_existing_point_3: Less custom code to maintain over time.
service_custom_software_custom_descripti: When the process is specialist, current limitations slow work down or the tool forms part of the value the business provides.
service_custom_software_custom_point_1: Workflows, permissions and data shaped around the real process.
service_custom_software_custom_point_2: Direct integration with the systems the team already uses.
service_custom_software_custom_point_3: Phased development based on usage and business priorities.
service_custom_software_solutions_title: Software for working, controlling and connecting.
service_custom_software_solutions_descri: The final form depends on the problem. These are common types of solution, but architecture is not decided by choosing a card from a catalogue.
service_custom_software_solution_interna: Applications for organising tasks, customers, documents, issues or any process currently scattered across email and spreadsheets.
service_custom_software_solution_platfor: Spaces with users, permissions, statuses and centralised information for teams, customers, suppliers or communities.
service_custom_software_solution_integra: Connections between services that share data, prevent duplication and remove manual steps that add no value.
service_custom_software_solution_logic_d: Configurators, generators, validation processes or rules engines that generic software cannot represent accurately.
service_custom_software_process_descript: The aim is to reach a useful version sooner, test the important decisions and reserve the larger investment for what has already proved worthwhile.
service_custom_software_step_1_descripti: I review people, steps, exceptions, data and current tools to separate the underlying problem from its symptoms.
service_custom_software_step_2_descripti: We prioritise the core that must work and explicitly record what is outside scope. Everything cannot be essential at the same time.
service_custom_software_step_3_descripti: I develop in stages and validate workflows with the people who will use them before months of untested decisions accumulate.
service_custom_software_step_4_descripti: I prepare testing, release, documentation and support so the system can grow from real usage rather than assumptions.
service_custom_software_projects_title: Three problems that did not fit a template.
service_custom_software_projects_descrip: An application launcher, a deployment-ready server and a bot with persistent data. Different products, each with logic of its own.
service_custom_software_includes_1: Analysis of the current process, users, permissions and data.
service_custom_software_includes_2: A prototype and definition of a useful first version.
service_custom_software_includes_3: Development of the platform, dashboard, API or integrations required.
service_custom_software_includes_4: Testing, deployment, documentation and later evolution.
service_custom_software_example_1: An internal dashboard centralising customers, tasks, documents and statuses currently scattered across email and spreadsheets.
service_custom_software_example_2: An integration that keeps services in sync and removes the need to copy information by hand every day.
service_custom_software_faq_1_question: Does everything need building from scratch?
service_custom_software_faq_1_answer: Not always. I first check whether an existing product, integration or small bespoke layer solves the problem. Building software for its own sake is an expensive way to decorate a CV.
service_custom_software_faq_2_question: Can we begin with a small version?
service_custom_software_faq_2_answer: Yes, and that is often the sensible route. We define a first version that solves the core problem and prioritise everything else for later development based on real use.
service_custom_software_faq_3_answer: We agree whether you need occasional support, a bank of hours or ongoing maintenance from the outset. Code, documentation and access are prepared so the system is not a black box.
service_custom_software_faq_4_question: How much does bespoke software cost?
service_custom_software_faq_4_answer: It depends on scope, users, data, integrations and technical risk. Before pricing the work, I define a first version and separate what is essential from what can evolve later.
service_custom_software_faq_5_question: Can it connect to the tools we already use?
service_custom_software_faq_5_answer: Usually, provided they offer an API or another reliable integration method. I review each system before committing to scope, because an integration is only as good as the access allowed at the other end.
service_custom_software_faq_6_question: Who owns the code and data?
service_custom_software_faq_6_answer: Project data and accounts remain under your control. Code ownership and handover are stated clearly in the proposal according to the type of solution, the licences used and the maintenance agreement.
service_apps_short: Mobile and desktop applications that put a service, process or product on the right device.
service_apps_meta_description: Mobile and desktop application development for Android, iOS, Windows, Linux and macOS, tailored to your project.
service_apps_lead: I build mobile and desktop applications that make proper use of the device without turning every platform into an entirely separate project.
service_apps_hero_description: Applications for Android, iOS, Windows, Linux and macOS, with a foundation shaped around the product and the device features it actually needs. Development from Galicia and remotely.
service_apps_overview_description: Installing an application only makes sense when it provides something the web cannot handle well: frequent access, offline work, system integration or an experience focused on a specific task. An icon on the desktop does not make a product by itself.
service_apps_problem: A website cannot always cover offline work, operating-system integration, notifications, local files or an intensive day-to-day experience. On the other hand, creating an app without a clear need adds publishing, updates and maintenance without solving anything new.
service_apps_audience: Businesses, professionals and products that need an application for customers, internal teams or a community across Android, iOS, Windows, Linux or macOS, with a use case that justifies putting it on the device.
service_apps_formats_description: The first decision is not the technology, but where and how the product will be used. Sometimes a good installable website solves more at a lower cost.
service_apps_format_web_description: For immediate access from any device, centralised updates and features that do not depend on deep operating-system integration.
service_apps_format_mobile_description: For frequent use on the move, camera, location, notifications, local data or an experience designed around the phone.
service_apps_format_desktop_description: For working with files, local processes, peripherals, updates or intensive workflows on Windows, Linux and macOS.
service_apps_architecture_title: Share the foundation without ignoring the device.
service_apps_architecture_description: A cross-platform solution can reduce cost and maintain consistency. When a feature needs specific integration, that part is treated as native rather than forced through an abstraction.
service_apps_shared_description: For products that share an interface, data and rules across several systems and do not need a completely separate implementation for each one.
service_apps_shared_point_1: Less duplication across platforms and releases.
service_apps_shared_point_2: Consistent behaviour and design on every device.
service_apps_shared_point_3: A foundation that is easier to test, maintain and evolve.
service_apps_native_description: For features that depend on the operating system, hardware or a level of performance that a shared layer cannot provide well.
service_apps_native_point_1: Access to files, notifications, camera or system processes.
service_apps_native_point_2: Behaviour adapted to the constraints of each platform.
service_apps_native_point_3: Specific code only where it provides a real advantage.
service_apps_process_title: From use case to installed application.
service_apps_process_description: Platform, distribution and synchronisation decisions are made before release. Improvising them once the app is finished tends to be an expensive hobby.
service_apps_step_1_description: We establish who uses it, on which device, how often and what they must be able to do with or without connectivity.
service_apps_step_2_description: I organise screens and interactions to validate the main journey before investing in the most expensive integrations.
service_apps_step_3_description: I develop the application and test permissions, data, performance and behaviour on real devices and operating systems.
service_apps_step_4_description: I prepare installers, store releases or private distribution, together with a clear strategy for errors, versions and updates.
service_apps_projects_title: Applications and foundations designed for several systems.
service_apps_projects_description: VS Launcher brings installation and updates to the desktop; xvelte provides a shared foundation for building web interfaces and applications with Tauri.
service_apps_includes_1: Platform selection, use cases and first-version scope.
service_apps_includes_2: A responsive interface consistent with the system and brand.
service_apps_includes_3: Integration with APIs, accounts, files, notifications or device features.
service_apps_includes_4: Packaging, testing, publishing or distribution, and update support.
service_apps_example_1: A desktop application managing installations, files and updates without requiring people to work from a terminal.
service_apps_example_2: A mobile app for checking information, receiving alerts and completing tasks away from the office.
service_apps_faq_1_answer: It depends on features, performance and target platforms. A shared foundation avoids duplicated cost when it suits the product; where a feature requires native code, I do not force it through an abstraction.
service_apps_faq_2_question: Do you also publish to app stores?
service_apps_faq_2_answer: I can prepare builds, listings and the publication process. Apple, Google or Microsoft accounts should remain in the client's name and their fees are billed directly.
service_apps_faq_3_answer: Yes, if the use case requires it. We need to define what is stored, how it synchronises and what happens when conflicting changes meet after connectivity returns.
service_apps_faq_4_question: How much does an application cost and how long does it take?
service_apps_faq_4_answer: It depends on the platforms, native features, backend, integrations and publication process. I first define a useful version and prepare a phased estimate rather than pricing it solely by screen count.
service_apps_faq_5_question: Can you also build the backend or API?
service_apps_faq_5_answer: Yes. If the application needs accounts, synchronisation, shared data or a management dashboard, I can build or integrate the required server-side work within the same project.
service_apps_faq_6_question: How are updates and maintenance handled?
service_apps_faq_6_answer: It depends on distribution: official stores, a built-in updater or internal installation. I can handle support and new releases while keeping accounts and access under your control.
service_automation_short: Bots, scripts and integrations that remove repetitive work and connect services that currently do not speak.
service_automation_meta_description: Discord bots, scripts, API integrations and bespoke automation for businesses, teams and online communities.
service_automation_lead: I automate repetitive work and build bots that respond, moderate, notify or coordinate processes without a person acting as a bridge all day.
service_automation_hero_description: Discord and Telegram bots, scripts, API integrations and automated processes for businesses, teams and communities. Development from Galicia and remotely.
service_automation_overview_description: Automation is not about hiding a problem behind a button. We need to define what triggers the process, which rules it follows, what happens in exceptional cases and who is alerted when things do not go as planned.
service_automation_problem: Copying data, checking events manually or repeating the same action daily consumes time and lets mistakes appear at precisely the least helpful moment. If the knowledge also lives in one person's head, the process stops whenever that person is unavailable.
service_automation_audience: Businesses with repetitive processes, teams that need to connect several tools, and communities requiring Discord or Telegram bots with their own permissions, data and behaviour.
service_automation_paths_title: Interact with a community or move a process.
service_automation_paths_description: A bot responds to people and events within a platform. Automation works between systems or performs a task when a condition is met. Sometimes both belong in the same project.
service_automation_bot_description: For communities and teams that need commands, alerts, moderation, queries or interactive workflows within Discord or Telegram.
service_automation_bot_point_1: Commands, menus, events and context-aware responses.
service_automation_bot_point_2: Permissions, roles, persistent data and community rules.
service_automation_bot_point_3: Integration with APIs, dashboards or external services.
service_automation_flow_description: For collecting, transforming or sending information without manually repeating the same steps across applications, files and services.
service_automation_flow_point_3: Alerts only when a person needs to review or decide.
service_automation_reliability_descripti: A useful process must show what it did, detect when it could not continue and let someone take back control. Running a script and trusting fate does not count as observability.
service_automation_reliability_rules_des: I define who can start each action, which conditions must be met and what data the system may read or modify.
service_automation_reliability_logs_desc: Activity, changes and results are recorded so a problem can be investigated without reconstructing the story from scattered screenshots.
service_automation_reliability_errors_de: Retries, alerts, limits and manual controls prevent a temporary failure from leaving partial data or looping forever with great enthusiasm.
service_automation_reliability_operation: I prepare execution, secrets, updates and monitoring so the process keeps working outside my computer.
service_automation_process_title: From repeated task to controlled process.
service_automation_process_description: Before automating, I check that the task is stable and that the savings justify building and maintaining the solution.
service_automation_step_1_description: I document inputs, steps, decisions, frequency and current effort to understand what can genuinely be automated.
service_automation_step_2_description: We agree permissions, edge cases and what should happen when data is missing or an external service does not respond.
service_automation_step_3_description: I develop the workflow with controlled data and environments before allowing it to act on real processes.
service_automation_step_4_description: I configure execution, logs, alerts and documentation to keep the process under control after launch.
service_automation_projects_title: Bots, scripts and systems that make work repeatable.
service_automation_projects_description: Modereta manages a community, VSDS automates a deployable server and Gallaecia Dots turns a complete configuration into a repeatable process.
service_automation_includes_1: Analysis of the task, rules, exceptions and permissions.
service_automation_includes_2: Discord or Telegram bots, scripts and API integrations.
service_automation_includes_3: Activity logs, alerts, error handling and manual controls.
service_automation_example_1: A Discord bot managing commands, favourites, automatic alerts and community-specific rules.
service_automation_example_2: A process collecting data from an API, transforming it and alerting the team only when something needs attention.
service_automation_faq_1_question: Can you build a private Discord bot?
service_automation_faq_1_answer: Yes. It can be limited to one server and use commands, menus, events, permissions and a database according to what the community or team needs.
service_automation_faq_2_question: Can an automation break when an API changes?
service_automation_faq_2_answer: It can. That is why I prepare logging, alerts and error handling, and explain the maintenance needed when external services may change.
service_automation_faq_3_answer: It is not always worthwhile. The task must be repetitive and stable enough. If automation costs more than the time it saves, the honest answer is not to build it.
service_automation_faq_4_question: Where does the bot or automation run?
service_automation_faq_4_answer: It can run on a server, a cloud service or a company computer depending on availability, data and integration requirements. Hosting and external costs are defined separately.
service_automation_faq_5_question: Can you maintain or improve an existing bot?
service_automation_faq_5_answer: Yes, after reviewing the code, dependencies, deployment and data. If phased repairs or a partial rewrite are safer, I explain that before touching production.
service_automation_faq_6_answer: It can when it adds value to a task that tolerates probabilistic results and includes suitable review. For exact rules or sensitive data, traditional automation is usually more predictable and less expensive.
service_it_short: Remote and on-site diagnosis, repair and IT support for businesses and individuals.
service_it_meta_description: IT technician in Salvaterra de Miño providing on-site support in Vigo, O Porriño, Tui, Ponteareas, Salceda and southern Galicia.
service_it_lead: I solve problems with computers, software, networks and devices through clear remote support or a visit to your home or business.
service_it_hero_description: IT support for individuals, freelancers and businesses, remotely or on site from Salvaterra de Miño across Salceda, Vigo, O Porriño, Tui, Ponteareas and nearby areas.
service_it_overview_description: When something fails, the first step is finding out whether the problem lies with the computer, software, network or configuration. Diagnosing before replacing parts avoids trial-and-error spending and the occasional unnecessary trip to an electronics shop.
service_it_problem: A slow computer, vanishing printer, failing application or unstable network can stop a home or business over a problem whose solution is sometimes considerably less dramatic. The difficult part is often finding the cause without making everything else worse along the way.
service_it_audience: Individuals, freelancers and businesses needing diagnosis, repair, configuration or help making an informed IT decision, whether for a one-off problem or when preparing a new computer.
service_it_modes_title: Remote when it is enough. On site when it is needed.
service_it_modes_description: I choose the support method according to the problem, not habit. If it can be solved safely remotely, we avoid travel; if hardware or cabling needs attention, I visit the site.
service_it_remote_description: For software, account, configuration and guidance issues where the computer starts and maintains a stable connection.
service_it_remote_point_1: Configuration of software, email, accounts and permissions.
service_it_remote_point_2: Diagnosis of errors, poor performance and system behaviour.
service_it_remote_point_3: Support without travel, regardless of location.
service_it_onsite_description: For computers that will not start, hardware, networking, printers, cabling or situations where inspecting the environment is part of the diagnosis.
service_it_onsite_point_1: Homes, offices, shops and small businesses.
service_it_onsite_point_2: Salvaterra de Miño, Salceda de Caselas, Vigo, O Porriño, Tui and Ponteareas.
service_it_onsite_point_3: Travel and any associated cost confirmed before the visit.
service_it_cases_title: From a slow computer to a complete workstation.
service_it_cases_description: I handle both specific incidents and preparation of new equipment. If a repair is not worthwhile, the right answer may also be to stop spending money on that repair.
service_it_case_performance_description: Slow computers, startup errors, overheating, low storage, troublesome updates or components that need inspection.
service_it_case_software_description: Installation, configuration and troubleshooting for operating systems, applications, email, users, permissions and online services.
service_it_case_devices_description: Printers, Wi-Fi, cabling, peripherals and computers that should communicate but have decided to lead separate lives.
service_it_case_data_description: Backups, migration to a new computer and data recovery where attempting it is technically viable and safe.
service_it_process_description: Before replacing parts or accumulating hours, I explain what I found, which options are available and what makes sense given the computer's condition and value.
service_it_step_1_description: I gather symptoms, error messages, the computer model and recent changes to choose the first check and the right type of support.
service_it_step_2_description: I inspect the system, hardware or network without changing things at random until the problem and any risk to the data are understood.
service_it_step_3_description: I clarify the repair, likely cost, alternatives and limits before buying parts or making significant changes.
service_it_step_4_description: I apply the agreed solution, verify that it works and explain what matters so the issue is not left wrapped in technical mystery.
service_it_includes_1: Diagnosis of slow computers, errors, startup issues, software and peripherals.
service_it_includes_2: Installation and configuration of systems, software, printers and devices.
service_it_includes_3: Cleaning, upgrades, backups, recovery and data migration where viable.
service_it_includes_4: Remote assistance or on-site visits to homes and businesses in the service area.
service_it_example_1: A computer that has slowed down, fails to start or needs its data moving to a new machine without leaving half a life behind.
service_it_example_2: A workstation with poorly configured email, printer, applications and backups that needs to be left working and understood.
service_it_faq_1_question: Do you visit homes and businesses?
service_it_faq_1_answer: Yes. I provide on-site support in Salvaterra de Miño, Salceda de Caselas, Vigo, O Porriño, Tui, Ponteareas and nearby areas. Travel and any distance-based charge are confirmed beforehand.
service_it_faq_2_question: Can you solve the problem remotely?
service_it_faq_2_answer: Many software, configuration and account issues can be resolved remotely. Hardware, cabling or a computer that will not start generally requires an in-person visit.
service_it_faq_3_question: Do you charge if the computer is beyond repair?
service_it_faq_3_answer: Diagnosis and travel are work even when a repair is not worthwhile. Before replacing parts or spending more time, I explain the options so you can make an informed decision.
service_it_faq_4_question: Will I know the cost before the repair?
service_it_faq_4_answer: I confirm known rates and travel before providing support. Where the cost depends on diagnosis, I explain the result and request approval before buying parts or continuing with more substantial work.
service_it_faq_5_question: What happens to my data and privacy?
service_it_faq_5_answer: I access only what is necessary to diagnose or carry out the agreed work. Before a risky operation, I recommend or prepare a backup where possible, but data recovery cannot be guaranteed without inspecting the device.
service_it_faq_6_question: Do you also install parts or prepare new computers?
service_it_faq_6_answer: Yes. I can recommend and install compatible upgrades, migrate data and configure a new computer. Hardware and licences are approved and paid for separately from the technical work.
service_it_maintenance_short: Preventive maintenance and ongoing support so a business's computers do not live permanently in emergency mode.
service_it_maintenance_meta_description: Business IT maintenance in Salvaterra de Miño and southern Galicia: computers, networks, backups, updates and support.
service_it_maintenance_lead: I keep computers, software, networks and backups under control to reduce incidents and respond with context when one appears.
service_it_maintenance_hero_description: IT maintenance for freelancers, offices and small businesses in Salvaterra de Miño and southern Galicia, with remote support and agreed on-site visits.
service_it_maintenance_overview_descript: Maintenance does not prevent every failure, but it reduces those that could have been anticipated and provides context when a problem appears. Knowing which computers exist, what changed and where the backups are saves a great deal of badly timed improvisation.
service_it_maintenance_problem: Dealing with IT only when everything stops is expensive: updates accumulate, backups go unchecked, computers lack order and access depends on one person's memory. Every incident then starts from scratch, even when it has happened before.
service_it_maintenance_audience: Freelancers, offices, shops and small businesses that do not need their own IT department but do need someone who knows their systems, documents what matters and provides continuity.
service_it_maintenance_coverage_title: Prevent, document and respond with context.
service_it_maintenance_coverage_descript: Scope adapts to the number of computers and the actual risk. The goal is not to touch everything each month, but to check what matters at the right frequency.
service_it_maintenance_coverage_inventor: A basic inventory, condition, age, warranty and known issues to decide what should be maintained, improved or replaced.
service_it_maintenance_coverage_systems_: Updates, accounts, permissions, licences and routine configuration to avoid every computer being solved in its own mysterious way.
service_it_maintenance_coverage_backups_: Review of backup strategy, alerts and recovery tests. A backup that has never been checked is more hope than plan.
service_it_maintenance_coverage_support_: Remote support, agreed visits, issue tracking and computer preparation so a new starter or change does not begin with improvisation.
service_it_maintenance_modes_title: Continuity without paying for cover you do not need.
service_it_maintenance_modes_description: The right option depends on computer count, incident frequency and the impact of downtime. Hours, priority and included tasks are agreed before starting.
service_it_maintenance_planned_descripti: For businesses needing recurring reviews, clear priorities and someone who retains context about their systems.
service_it_maintenance_planned_point_1: Reviews at a frequency agreed according to risk.
service_it_maintenance_planned_point_2: Priority and response times defined in the service.
service_it_maintenance_planned_point_3: Tracking for incidents, changes and outstanding work.
service_it_maintenance_hours_description: For businesses with less frequent needs that want reserved support without broad monthly cover.
service_it_maintenance_hours_point_1: Hours used for support, configuration or reviews.
service_it_maintenance_hours_point_2: Clear records of usage and completed work.
service_it_maintenance_hours_point_3: Renewal based on actual usage, without invented lock-ins.
service_it_maintenance_process_descripti: You cannot maintain what you do not know. The service begins with a basic picture of the current state and evolves according to priorities, not a generic checklist applied identically to everyone.
service_it_maintenance_step_1_descriptio: I identify computers, users, software, networking, backups and recurring issues to understand what exists and its current condition.
service_it_maintenance_step_2_descriptio: I separate urgent risks, recommended improvements and work that can wait, so everything does not become a false emergency.
service_it_maintenance_step_3_descriptio: I carry out the agreed work and record configurations and changes that will help at the next review or incident.
service_it_maintenance_step_4_descriptio: I review outstanding work, incidents and new requirements to adapt frequency and scope to the business's actual usage.
service_it_maintenance_includes_1: A basic inventory, condition review and priorities for each computer.
service_it_maintenance_includes_2: Updates, security, users, software and routine configuration.
service_it_maintenance_includes_3: Backups, checks and guidance for recovering information.
service_it_maintenance_includes_4: Remote support, agreed visits and incident follow-up.
service_it_maintenance_example_1: A small office needing regular checks of computers, accounts, backups and networking instead of waiting for the next failure.
service_it_maintenance_example_2: A business with one point of contact for incidents, new workstations and documentation of important configurations.
service_it_maintenance_faq_1_question: Does maintenance require a monthly fee?
service_it_maintenance_faq_1_answer: It can be a subscription, a bank of hours or scheduled reviews. The right model depends on computer count and actual support needs; there is no point paying for cover you do not need.
service_it_maintenance_faq_2_answer: Yes. I handle general emergencies for both one-off customers and maintenance clients. Customers with a maintenance contract receive priority according to the agreed terms. Hours and response times are confirmed for each case; I do not offer 24/7 cover that does not exist.
service_it_maintenance_faq_3_question: Do you also maintain websites and online stores?
service_it_maintenance_faq_3_answer: Yes, but I separate that from computer maintenance because the work and risks differ. We can combine both in a clear proposal rather than hiding everything in one mysterious invoice line.
service_it_maintenance_faq_4_question: What determines the cost of maintenance?
service_it_maintenance_faq_4_answer: The number and type of computers, locations, review frequency, support hours and included tasks. I first review the environment and prepare a proposal with a specific scope.
service_it_maintenance_faq_5_question: Do backups guarantee that data will never be lost?
service_it_maintenance_faq_5_answer: No system removes all risk. A good strategy combines several copies, alerts and regular recovery tests to detect failures before the data is genuinely needed.
service_it_maintenance_faq_6_question: Can support be both remote and on site?
service_it_maintenance_faq_6_answer: Yes. I resolve work remotely where physical presence is unnecessary and arrange visits for hardware, networking or reviews. On-site support covers Salvaterra de Miño, Salceda, Vigo, O Porriño, Tui, Ponteareas and nearby areas.
